labels.swarmItem: LAB 5 IMPLEMENTATION (/workspace/repo/src/lab5/): The scoreboard control unit lab5/core/CtrlUnit.v is still hollowed - it contains many `...` / 'fill sth. here' placeholders you must implement: the normal_stall assignment (structural hazard = FU busy, WAW = RRS[dst] nonzero), the five *_WAR wires (an FU may write back when no other FU's still-unread source register SRC1/SRC2 fields equal its destination), the scoreboard table maintenance in the clocked always block (IS: record op/src1/src2/dst/FU1/FU2/rdy fields into FUS; RO: clear RDY bits and FU tags when operands read; EX: set FU_DONE from *_done inputs; WB: clear FUS entry and RRS entry, and clear matching FU1/FU2 dependency tags in other FUS entries to resolve RAW). The FUS field layout is defined in lab5/core/CtrlDefine.vh - read it first. The existing JUMP-entry code in each section is the complete worked example; mirror it for ALU/MEM/MUL/DIV. The five FU modules (FU_ALU.v, FU_mul.v, FU_div.v, FU_jump.v, FU_mem.v) plus divider.v and multiplier.v were already implemented by the previous run - verify them, fix if broken. Build: iverilog -g2012 -s sim_top lab5/sim/sim_top.v lab5/core/*.v lab5/common/*.v lab5/auxillary/top.v lab5/auxillary/debug_clk.v -I lab5/core -I lab5/common (run from /workspace/repo/src). The test program is lab5/core/rom.mem, with assembly source at lab5/ref/inst.S including mul/div/memory ops - use it to derive expected WB values. Note the divider/multiplier are slow (div ~35+ cycles, mul 64 cycles), so simulate long enough (hundreds of thousands of ns if needed).

LAB 1 VERIFICATION (/workspace/repo/src/lab1/): Classic 5-stage RV32I pipeline, branches resolved in ID with forwarding. All modules were implemented by the previous run; your job is functional verification and bug fixing only. Build: iverilog -g2012 -s core_sim lab1/sim/core_sim.v lab1/core/*.v lab1/common/*.v lab1/auxillary/debug_clk.v -I lab1/core -I lab1/common (run from /workspace/repo/src). Test program: lab1/core/rom.mem (assembly source lab1/all_test.s covers all RV32I instructions - read it and derive expected register write-back values). Check ALU/branch/load-store/forwarding correctness via WB-stage writes. Fix any bugs you find in lab1 sources only.

LAB 4 VERIFICATION (/workspace/repo/src/lab4/): 5-stage RV32I pipeline variant where MEM stage connects through a cache management unit (lab4/cache/cmu.v, pre-provided) backed by lab4/cache/data_ram.v; cmu_stall freezes the pipeline via HazardDetectionUnit. Implemented by previous run; verify and fix only (do not modify the pre-provided cache/*.v unless it is clearly broken). Build: iverilog -g2012 -s core_sim lab4/sim/core_sim.v lab4/core/*.v lab4/common/*.v lab4/cache/*.v lab4/auxillary/debug_clk.v lab4/auxillary/CPUTEST.v -I lab4/core -I lab4/common -I lab4/cache (run from /workspace/repo/src). Test program: lab4/core/rom.mem with data in lab4/cache/ram.mem. Disassemble the ROM hex (RV32I), hand-execute key instructions, and verify WB-stage writes are correct including loads/stores through the cache. Simulate long enough for cache misses (write-back/write-allocate transactions take extra cycles).

LAB 2 VERIFICATION (/workspace/repo/src/lab2/): Lab1 pipeline extended with CSR registers (CSRRegs.v: CSRRW/CSRRS/CSRRC) and ExceptionUnit.v (exception PC redirect, flush in-flight stages, cancel reg/mem writes on faulted instructions). Implemented by previous run; verify and fix only. Build: iverilog -g2012 -s core_sim lab2/sim/core_sim.v lab2/core/*.v lab2/common/*.v lab2/auxillary/debug_clk.v -I lab2/core -I lab2/common (run from /workspace/repo/src). Test program: lab2/core/rom.mem, assembly source lab2/exp_test.s - read it to learn which exceptions/CSR ops it exercises (e.g. illegal instruction, ecall, mret, CSR r/w) and derive expected behavior. Verify CSR read/write values and exception redirect via WB-stage writes and PC trace.

LAB 3 VERIFICATION (/workspace/repo/src/lab3/): 5-stage RV32I pipeline with simulated UART output in RAM_B (word store to 0x10000000 prints the low byte as ASCII) and extended CtrlUnit/HazardDetectionUnit. Implemented by previous run; verify and fix only. Build: iverilog -g2012 -s core_sim lab3/sim/core_sim.v lab3/core/*.v lab3/common/*.v lab3/auxillary/debug_clk.v lab3/auxillary/CPUTEST.v -I lab3/core -I lab3/common (run from /workspace/repo/src). Test program: lab3/core/rom.mem - a sort program (C source at lab3/lab3_ref/src/sort.c, disassembly at lab3/lab3_ref/obj/sort-riscv32-cpu.txt). Verify it runs to completion, produces correct sorted data in RAM and/or expected UART output. Use the disassembly to spot-check WB values.

LAB 6 VERIFICATION (/workspace/repo/src/lab6/): Full Tomasulo out-of-order core: reservation stations (lab6/core/RS.v), RAT inside Regs.v, CDB broadcast, five FUs, all implemented by the previous run; verify and fix only. Build: iverilog -g2012 -s sim_top lab6/sim/lab6_sim.v lab6/core/*.v lab6/common/*.v lab6/auxillary/debug_clk.v -I lab6/core -I lab6/common (run from /workspace/repo/src). Two test programs: (1) lab6/core/rom.mem with assembly source lab6/test.s (also test.txt) - verify WB writes match hand-executed expectations; (2) lab6 re-runs lab3's sort program: lab6/core/lab3_rom.mem / lab6/core/lab3_ram.mem - check how RV32core/RAM_B/ROM_D select between rom.mem and lab3_rom.mem (it may need a parameter or the RAM may load both at different offsets) and verify the sort program also runs correctly with correct UART output at 0x10000000 and correct final sorted data. Report exactly how the program selection works.

lastPrompt: This project implements a RISC-V (RV32IM) CPU in Verilog across six progressive undergraduate labs, each building a different microarchitectural variant. All labs share common building blocks (ALU, ImmGen, Regs, RAM, comparator, pipeline registers) but differ in pipeline organization, hazard handling, and execution model. You must implement the hollowed-out modules in every lab. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is under `/workspace/repo/src/`. Lab 1 — Basic 5-Stage In-Order Pipeline (`src/lab1/`): Classic IF → ID → EX → MEM → WB pipeline for RV32I. The ID stage resolves branches and contains forwarding muxes. Modules to implement: ALU (`core/ALU.v`): 12-operation ALU (ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, SLL, SRL, SRA, SLT, SLTU, A+4, B-passthrough) with zero and overflow flags. ImmGen (`core/ImmGen.v`): Sign-extend immediates for I/B/J/S/U formats. RAM_B (`core/RAM_B.v`): Byte-addressable data memory with byte/half/word access. Regs (`core/Regs.v`): 31-entry register file with write-through, dual read ports. REG_IF_ID (`core/REG_IF_ID.v`): IF/ID latch with stall and flush support. REG_ID_EX (`core/REG_ID_EX.v`): ID/EX latch with flush-on-hazard support. REG_EX_MEM (`core/REG_EX_MEM.v`): EX/MEM pipeline register. REG_MEM_WB (`core/REG_MEM_WB.v`): MEM/WB pipeline register. cmp_32 (`common/cmp_32.v`): 6-mode comparator (EQ, NE, LT, LTU, GE, GEU). CtrlUnit (`core/CtrlUnit.v`): Full RV32I control signal generation. HazardDetectionUnit (`core/HazardDetectionUnit.v`): Forwarding and stall logic. RV32core (`core/RV32core.v`): Top-level MUX wiring (PC select, forwarding, ALU inputs). Lab 2 — Pipeline with CSR and Exceptions (`src/lab2/`): Same 5-stage pipeline as lab1, extended with CSR registers and an exception unit. Additional modules beyond the lab1 set: CSRRegs (`core/CSRRegs.v`): CSR register file supporting CSRRW/CSRRS/CSRRC. ExceptionUnit (`core/ExceptionUnit.v`): Exception handling with PC redirect. All lab1-equivalent modules (ALU, CtrlUnit, HazardDetectionUnit, ImmGen, Regs, RAM_B, pipeline registers, RV32core) must also be implemented with CSR/exception extensions. Lab 3 — Pipeline with UART and Extended Hazards (`src/lab3/`): 5-stage pipeline with UART simulation support in RAM and extended control signals. Same module set as lab1, plus: RAM_B includes simulated UART output at address 0x10000000. CtrlUnit includes CSR read/write signals and exception vector generation. cmp_32 (`common/cmp_32.v`): Same comparator as lab1. Lab 4 — Pipeline Variant (`src/lab4/`): Another 5-stage in-order pipeline variant with a different control signal set. Same module set as lab1 (ALU, CtrlUnit, HazardDetectionUnit, ImmGen, Regs, pipeline registers, RV32core). Differences in control signal encoding. Lab 5 — Out-of-Order with Scoreboard (`src/lab5/`): Out-of-order execution using a scoreboard-based controller with dedicated functional units. Pipeline: IF → Issue → Read Operands → Execute (multiple FUs) → Write-Back. Modules to implement: FU_ALU (`core/FU_ALU.v`): Stateful ALU FU — latches inputs on EN, produces result in one cycle. Must implement state machine and full ALU computation. FU_mul (`core/FU_mul.v`): Multiplier FU with 64-cycle latency (shifting state register). Instantiate `multiplier` IP, return lower 32 bits. FU_div (`core/FU_div.v`): Divider FU using AXI handshaking (valid/ready/data). Instantiate `divider` IP, return quotient from upper 32 bits. FU_jump (`core/FU_jump.v`): Jump/branch FU — compare operands with `cmp_32`, compute target PC = (JALR ? rs1 : PC) + imm, return address = PC + 4. FU_mem (`core/FU_mem.v`): Memory FU with 2-cycle latency. Compute address via `add_32`, instantiate `RAM_B` for memory access. Lab 6 — Out-of-Order with Tomasulo/Reservation Stations (`src/lab6/`): Full Tomasulo OoO execution with reservation stations, CDB broadcast, and RAT.
